page: Vultr voc-c-4c-8gb-75s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache pool. Hardware vector extensions are well represented with AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16 support, alongside cryptographic acceleration through AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is provisioned with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU, and bundles 75 GB of local NVMe SSD storage along with a single complimentary public IPv4 address. No dedicated hardware GPUs are attached to this configuration.

Benchmark results reveal strong single-thread execution efficiency, with stress-ng single-core scores reaching the top 10% and Geekbench single-core results placing in the top 25%. Single-threaded compression workflows also perform well, logging 31.73 GB/sec in gzip testing. Memory write bandwidth for large blocks (256 MB) remains strong at 111.47 GB/sec, while read performance across cached and uncached sets delivers median figures. Conversely, multi-threaded scalability shows limitations given the four-thread ceiling: Geekbench multi-core and stress-ng multi-core tests land in the middle 50%, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark database operations fall into the lower quartile. Machine learning inference on medium-sized models (7B) is restricted by available memory and compute breadth, resulting in weak token generation speeds.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation provides qualitative cost efficiency for execution pathways prioritized around raw processing capability rather than large memory footprints. By dedicating physical execution threads without oversubscription, it delivers predictable execution times for compute-bound stages. The bundled NVMe volume supports fast local file access without separate network storage latency. Given its balance of single-core performance and moderate memory density, Vultr voc-c-4c-8gb-75s-amd is suited for CI/CD compilation runners, batch compression jobs, worker nodes handling algorithmic tasks, and stateless web API backends.
description: Vultr voc-c-4c-8gb-75s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring 4 dedicated AMD EPYC vCPUs across 2 physical cores at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 8.0 GB of memory and 75 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with 32 MB of L3 cache, the processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 VNNI and BF16 for optimized vector math, as well as hardware AES encryption. In benchmark tests, the instance demonstrates top-tier single-core compute performance, alongside strong single-threaded gzip compression and large-block memory write bandwidth. However, overall multi-threaded throughput and database operations score in average to weak tiers, reflecting the 4-thread boundary and 2 GB RAM-per-vCPU compute-heavy profile. This configuration offers solid cost efficiency for CPU-bound pipelines that do not require high memory density, making it well suited for continuous integration runners, lightweight compilation tasks, microservices, and compute-focused backend processing.
